name: Motor-Driven Cycle
description: A cycle whose motor produces 5 brake horsepower (3,750 W) or less as manufactured and that meets federal motor vehicle safety standards; an electric one that can exceed 30 mph or has wheels of 20 inches or more lands here rather than as a moped.

restrictions.rule: Its motor produces 5 brake horsepower (3,750 W) or less as originally manufactured; ITD's rider handbook puts the electric line at under 3,729 W (Idaho Code §49-114(13))
Meets federal motor vehicle safety standards as originally designed; a two-wheeler built for off-road use that doesn't is a motorbike instead (Idaho Code §49-114(13))
Not a moped or an electric-assisted bicycle (Idaho Code §49-114(13))
Titled, and registered and plated for highway use, or instead issued a restricted vehicle plate or an OHV sticker for OHV roads and trails only (Idaho Code §49-114(13))
Riders need a valid driver's license with a motorcycle "M" endorsement (Idaho Code §49-114(13))
An applicant under 21 must complete an approved motorcycle rider training course to get the endorsement
With highway plates, may be ridden on all highways, including interstates
